The on-site rail tracks will be perpendicular to the existing rail line south of the site, necessitating a 90- degree turn for access. The standard rail gauge in the US is 4 feet 8.5 inches, with a minimum turn radius of 88 meters for non-general service. This minimum turn radius has been adopted to maximize the number of rail cars on site. The turn radius is primarily determined by the operating speed and the train's ability to handle curves. Preliminary indication indicates that 25,800 gal class-105 tank cars can accommodate curves tighter than the 88m base estimate. As a result an additional six rail tanks could potentially be accommodated on a third parallel track, which can be further explored during the FEED Page75 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version phase in conjunction with the minimum turn radius verification with the rail line operator (CSX) to ensure it is adequate for the size of rail cars and the speed of loading and unloading. On the north side of the rail car area there will be a pipe rack that travels to and from the Berth. This rack will be protected from collisions with the end rail cars by track rail stops. Figure 4.22: T-RICH Rail Line Configuration Page76 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 4.5.11 SITE BUILDINGS The current site layout includes two main buildings. The security building is situated at the primary site entrance, providing gated access via two roadways. The second building is the main site building, which will serve as an administrative, electrical, and workshop area. The workshop area, located on the lower level, will feature a two-bay garage to accommodate larger vehicles and maintenance equipment, with overhead crane capabilities. The electrical area will primarily house large VFDs and transformers on the lower level, with switchgear and power distribution boards on the second level. Variable Frequency Drives for compressor motors of this size are quite substantial. Additional space has been allocated for future expansion of electrical equipment. The administrative area, located on the second level, will include 8'x8' cubicles, a boardroom, kitchen, and washroom facilities. The upper level of the administrative building will also function as a temporary safe refuge in the event of an incident, such as a CO leak. 2 South of the administrative building is a sub-station area. This area will accommodate the main utility incomer switchgear, input transformer for VFD compressors, main incoming power transformers, and neutral ground resistors. These components do not need to be housed indoors and are therefore located outside the main administration/electrical building.
